title: Merkle-anchored rotation signer for offline HSM proof
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Background: Enterprise customers and auditors are asking for tamper-evident rotation proofs from HSM-backed key rotations that can be verified independently of Redwood's control plane. Current evidence artifacts consist of rotation logs and signer metadata, which are sufficient for many audits but do not provide a compact, verifiable anchor that external auditors or customers can replay without deep control-plane access.

Goal: Build a reusable component that: (1) collects rotation events from our KEK/KMS orchestration, (2) produces a Merkle-tree batch anchor for a set of rotation events, (3) has the root signed by an offline HSM signer (or HSM-backed signer service), and (4) publishes compact signed proofs + an append-only ledger entry for long-term auditability. The signed root plus the per-rotation Merkle inclusion proofs should let auditors verify that a rotation event existed in a particular anchored batch without needing access to internal logs.

Scope: Proof generation and storage; signer integration (HSM and HSM-fallback); CLI tooling for proof extraction; end-to-end testing harness. Not in scope: UI/Console UX for browsing proofs (follow-up ticket), full cross-region replication of the ledger (minimal replication only).
acceptance_criteria:
- For any KEK rotation event emitted by the orchestrator, a corresponding leaf is created in the Merkle batch within 15 minutes.
- The batch root is signed by an HSM key (or a designated fallback signing key) and the signature is stored with the batch entry.
- There is a deterministic, verifiable inclusion proof (proof path) for every rotation leaf returned by the CLI.
- Signed proofs and batches are immutable after commit and retained according to retention policy (default 7 years for enterprise).
- Integration tests that simulate HSM offline signing (mock + hardware-in-the-loop) pass in CI and a runbook exists for TTR when HSM is unavailable.
- Security review completed and internal KMS/HSM audit checklist items resolved.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions and options considered: 
- Merkle tree batching cadence: 5min vs 15min vs threshold-by-leaf-count. Chosen: hybrid: 5min fixed cadence, immediate flush if >250 leaves. Rationale: limits proof size and tail latency while avoiding small-batch churn.
- Signer model: prefer HSM-resident private key used to sign roots. Fallback: an FIPS 140-2 HSM-backed cloud signer service with strict attestations. Fallback signatures are annotated in metadata and require additional reviewer approval for high-sensitivity rotations.
- Ledger backend: append-only blob storage (S3/GCS) with SHA256 content-addressing + per-batch metadata in our audit DB. Rationale: simple durability and easy export. Future: migrate to a public append-only log (transparency log) if customers demand external witnesses.
- Offline signing flow: a signer agent will pull unsigned roots, sign using HSM, and push signature. Agent supports both online HSM connection and an air-gapped USB HSM signing mode with an encrypted manifest export for manual signing.
- Key provenance: signature keys are separate from production KEKs; rotation of the signer key is itself recorded as a special rotation leaf with its own proof.

Trade-offs: Building Merkle proofs increases storage for inclusion paths (~log(n) per leaf), but drastically reduces trust surface for external auditors. The hybrid batching cadence balances latency vs proof growth. Offline HSM mode adds operational complexity for enterprise customers but is a requirement for air-gapped audits.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for Merkle tree builder, deterministic across languages (JS/Python) and framework versions.
- Integration tests: simulate high-throughput rotation bursts to validate batching and flush heuristics.
- HIL tests: run hardware-in-the-loop with a YubiHSM2 and a cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM) to validate signing API, latency, and failure modes.
- Fallback tests: simulate HSM downtime and verify fallback signer path, metadata annotation, and alerting.
- End-to-end replay test: generate a sequence of rotations, export proofs, run auditor verification script (idempotent) that checks inclusion and root signature.
- Retention tests: verify immutable commit semantics and purging policies obey retention windows.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial RFC drafted and reviewed with Crypto and Compliance (link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CRYPTO/Merkle+Anchored+Rotation+Proofs). Decision: proceed with hybrid cadence.

2026-02-19: Prototype Merkle builder implemented (Go). Benchmarks show 3x faster proof generation vs naive tree for 10k leaves. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rotation-proofs/tree/proto-merkle

2026-02-26: Security review kickoff. Claire Huang requested explicit threat model for fallback signer and key compromise scenarios. Action: add signer key-rotation leaf type and emergency revocation flow.

- Assignee: Sana Iqbal to own HIL test harness setup.

2026-03-05: First end-to-end demo with mock offline signer completed for Compliance. Demo recording and artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/rotation-proofs-demo. Compliance requested retention extension option and per-tenant opt-out gating (logged to follow-up PM ticket).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: HSM unavailability delays proof signing -> Mitigation: fallback signer with clear metadata and alerting plus manual signing runbook.
Risk: Large batches increase storage/cost -> Mitigation: hybrid cadence and optional per-customer batch sizing via policy.
Risk: Signer key compromise -> Mitigation: signer-key rotations are recorded as special leaves; perform cross-signing and rapid revocation process; emergency notarization flow.
deliverables: Merkle batching service + API (produce unsigned root + leaf inclusion paths)
HSM signer agent supporting online and offline modes
CLI for auditors to retrieve and verify proofs
CI HIL tests and runbook for manual offline signing
Audit DB schema changes and S3-based immutable batch storage
